text.p: John Smoltz allowed five hits over eight innings and Javier Lopez snapped a tie with a two-run single in the eighth to lift the Atlanta Braves to a 4-2 victory over the St Louis Cardinals in the National League Championship Series opener Wednesday.
The defending World Series champion Braves remained unbeaten in four playoff games with the same formula -- outstanding pitching and clutch hitting.
Game 2 is Thursday night at Atlanta, where the Braves have won eight straight post-season games.
Mark Wohlers powered through the ninth in eight pitches and has saved all four wins. Atlanta has allowed just seven runs -- five earned -- in 37 innings, a 1.22 post-season ERA.
Smoltz, who won 24 games during the season and another in the Division Series sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers, improved to 7-1 all-time in the post-season.

The runaway favourite for the N.L. Cy Young Award walked two and struck out six, pitching out of a big jam in the seventh, when St Louis tied it. However, the Cardinals might have cost themselves two runs and the lead simply by not bunting.

Singles by Gary Gaetti, John Mabry and Tom Pagnozzi scored pinch-runner Miguel Mejia with the tying run. Luis Alicea could have moved the runners into scoring position with a sacrifice, but swung at the first pitch and hit a lazy fly to left.

Pinch-hitter Willie McGee followed with a flyout to deep left that would have easily scored a runner from third. Alicea's fly loomed even larger when Smoltz uncorked a wild pitch before getting Ozzie Smith to ground out.

Mark Lemke, who had a two-run single in the fifth, opened the eighth for Atlanta by drawing a walk from loser Mark Petkovsek, who then slipped coming off the mound to field a bunt by Chipper Jones, who had four hits in the game.
Petkovsek gloved the ball and threw to first, but second baseman Alicea was late covering and the ball got away behind the bag, putting runners at first and third.

Left-hander Tony Fossas came on and Jones stole second. Fossas got Fred McGriff to pop out. T.J. Mathews intentionally walked pinch-hitter Terry Pendleton to load the bases, then got two quick strikes on Lopez, who slapped a single up the middle, scoring two runs.
Lopez has only three hits in the playoffs, but two have won games. He hit a 10th-inning homer to give Smoltz a win in the opener of the Division Series.
Smoltz moved past Steve Carlton as the all-time NLCS leader in innings pitched with 58.

Petkovsek had relieved starter Andy Benes, who allowed two runs and seven hits in six innings, striking out seven and walking one. Four Cardinals pitchers held the Braves without a homer for the first time in 13 post-season games.
St Louis took the lead in the second when Brian Jordan led off with a triple and scored on a wild pitch.

The Braves grabbed the lead in the fifth. With one out, Jeff Blauser singled for his first hit in 37 at-bats against Benes. Smoltz struck out bunting, but Marquis Grissom doubled and Lemke singled to right-centre, plating a pair.
